name: Aura
tagline: Identity theft monitoring, credit tools, antivirus, VPN, and family safety

pricing.notes: Working normalization from the official public pricing structure. Recheck the source page immediately before publication.

tiers.notes: Annual price is shown as a monthly equivalent.

tiers.name: Family

tiers.notes: Annual price is shown as a monthly equivalent.

tiers.name: Kids
tiers.limits: Unlimited children and devices with family-safety features
tiers.notes: Annual price is shown as a monthly equivalent.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual plans have a 60-day money-back guarantee
pricing.hiddenCosts: Sales tax can be added; insurance and reimbursement are subject to policy eligibility, limits and exclusions, and the advertised annual figures require paying the year upfront

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Aura's durable value is security, infrastructure, trust, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a local diagnostic or backup companion for identity protection; do not claim to replace audited security, identity, VPN, or cloud-storage infrastructure.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: global network or redundant storage infrastructure
whyPeopleStillPay: Aura: Security subscriptions buy professional operations, audits, response capacity, redundancy, and accountability when something goes wrong.
ongoingBurden: Own threat modelling, key management, patching, backups, restore tests, incident response, privacy requests, and dependency security.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Bitwarden Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A very good password manager; identity monitoring, credit tools, antivirus, VPN, and family safety remain missing.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Malwarebytes Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: An on-demand malware cleaner is one small slice of Aura, not the identity-and-family suite.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Proton Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Mail, drive, passwords, and VPN are free; credit monitoring, antivirus, and family safety are not.

notes: Credibility row: Aura survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Aura; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Go 1.24 + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a local diagnostic or backup companion for identity protection; do not claim to replace audited security, identity, VPN, or cloud-storage infrastructure.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: global network or redundant storage infrastructure; identity, credit, or broker-removal operations; recovery guarantees and regulated trust.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
